source.snippet: I have a flow that updates a large group of records of various tables and moves them from one Asset to another. I want the user to be able to 'undo' this at a later time, possibly much later but no later than the agreed upon 18 months. I want to do so without a new field to all the tables. One idea I cooked up is to use history tracking. To make sure the History records I find were part of the same update I want to look at the CreatedDate. I know the docs say: 'Salesforce doesn't guarantee that...'

problem_statement: Salesforce developers need reliable bulk-operation undo/rollback capabilities spanning 18 months, but native history tracking timestamps are not guaranteed to be precise enough to correlate batched changes — forcing fragile workarounds instead of a proper audit-and-rollback mechanism.
target_segment: Salesforce developers and architects at companies running complex bulk data operations and asset migrations
notes: Developer is building a business-critical undo feature for bulk record moves across multiple objects, with an 18-month retention requirement agreed upon with users — indicating a formal business requirement, not a hobby project. The workaround involves fragile timestamp correlation against a platform that explicitly does not guarantee ordering. Existing Salesforce deployment/data tools (Gearset, Copado, OwnBackup) charge enterprise rates, confirming buyers pay for data-safety tooling in this ecosystem.
